official.deadline_note: Application window runs 1 February to 19 March 2027 (AY2027). The Referee Recommendation Form must be submitted via the Referee Portal by 2 April 2027, and the NUS admission application must be submitted before the scholarship application.
official.application_cycle: AY2027 intake; one common application covers all three NUS Scholarships tiers
official.status_note: Official page states: 'Application for NUS Scholarships for AY2027 commences from 1 February to 19 March 2027. Only one common scholarship application is required.' The window opens 1 February 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published benefit wording: 'Subsidised tuition fees (after MOE Tuition Grant subsidy)'.
benefits: Subsidised tuition fees (after MOE Tuition Grant subsidy)
Guaranteed Student Exchange Programme (SEP) placement with one of NUS overseas partner universities for one semester (not applicable for NUS Medicine and Dentistry undergraduate programmes)

Priority for on-campus accommodation for the first two years of undergraduate study, subject to meeting the eligibility criteria for on-campus accommodation and submitting a complete hostel application during the first housing application window each year (Year 1: Halls and Houses; Year 2: Halls, Houses and Residences)
eligibility: Applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at NUS; transfer applicants from local or overseas universities are not eligible
Possess outstanding Singapore-Cambridge GCE A Level, local Polytechnic Diploma, International Baccalaureate Diploma, NUS High School Diploma or equivalent qualifications
Have strong leadership qualities and potential
requirements: Submit an application for admission to NUS before submitting the scholarship application
Submit one online scholarship application with supporting documents via the Applicant Portal within the application window
Scholarship recipients may not concurrently hold any other scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award, allowance, waiver or free aid without prior approval from the University

The scholarship is renewed every semester, provided the recipient maintains a GPA of at least 3.50, or grades within the top 80% of the cohort for Dentistry, Law and Medicine recipients, and has good conduct
Be available for selection interviews from late March onwards; the application is withdrawn if a scheduled interview is missed without valid reason
documents: Supporting documents such as the co-curricular activities record, uploaded at the Applicant Portal
One Referee Recommendation Form submitted online separately by the applicant's Junior College/Polytechnic/High School Principal or Tutor via the Referee Portal
An admission application to NUS, which must be submitted before the scholarship application
selection_criteria: Performance in the scholarship selection interview(s), if shortlisted

Applicants with Dentistry/Medicine/Law top choices shortlisted for those admission tests/interviews are assessed on performance in those tests/interviews instead, with further scholarship interviews possible
NUS reserves the right to not award any scholarship if there are no candidates of sufficient merit; the selection committee's decision is final
coverage: Subsidised tuition fees (after MOE Tuition Grant subsidy)
One-semester SEP placement at an NUS overseas partner university (placement only; no exchange costs are stated as covered)
Priority consideration for on-campus accommodation for the first two years of undergraduate study
No living allowance, stipend or travel funding is published for this tier
application_method: Submit an application for admission to NUS first
Submit the online scholarship application with supporting documents via the Applicant Portal between 1 February and 19 March 2027 (one common application for all three NUS Scholarships tiers)
Remind the referee to complete and submit the Referee Recommendation Form via the Referee Portal before 2 April 2027
Attend selection interview(s) from late March onwards if shortlisted, and check the Applicant Portal for the outcome by late May
Indicate acceptance online and sign the Letter of Acceptance and Undertaking via the Applicant Portal to finalise acceptance
official.application_route: One common online scholarship application via the NUS Applicant Portal after the NUS admission application, open 1 February to 19 March 2027.
official.international_eligibility: Not eligible; open to Singapore Citizens only
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The one-semester SEP placement benefit is not applicable for NUS Medicine and Dentistry undergraduate programmes; the renewal GPA rule differs for Dentistry, Law and Medicine recipients (top 80% of cohort instead of 3.50).
official.duration: Tenable for the normal candidature period of the full-time undergraduate degree, renewed every semester
official.description: Highly coveted NUS Scholarships awarded to high calibre individuals who demonstrate academic excellence, an excellent co-curricular activities record and outstanding leadership qualities; NUS Scholars are expected to contribute to the NUS community and develop into dynamic global leaders capable of effecting positive societal change.
official.program_type: University-Level undergraduate scholarship (entry tier of the NUS Scholarships for freshmen)

verification.notes: Benefits, eligibility, terms and conditions, documents, selection process and the AY2027 window were confirmed on the NUS Office of Admissions' own pages; the official scholarship page publishes no monetary figure and no English language requirement, so living cost and travel coverage are recorded as false because the published benefit list contains neither.

applicant_utility.summary: This is the entry tier of NUS's three-tier NUS Scholarships for Singapore Citizen freshmen, and one common application puts you in consideration for every tier at once. The award is entirely tuition-side: your subsidised fees after the MOE Tuition Grant are covered, alongside a guaranteed one-semester exchange placement (Medicine and Dentistry excluded), two years of hostel priority, and no bond. There is no living allowance, so food, transport and exchange costs remain on your own budget, and renewal every semester depends on holding a GPA of at least 3.50.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Singapore Citizen school leavers with strong A-Level, polytechnic, IB or NUS High School results plus a documented leadership and co-curricular record, entering a full-time NUS degree outside Medicine and Dentistry.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the NUS admission application first; the scholarship form only becomes available after it
Assemble your co-curricular record and leadership evidence for upload to the Applicant Portal before the window opens on 1 February 2027
Brief your JC/polytechnic/high school principal or tutor early; their Referee Recommendation Form must reach the Referee Portal by 2 April 2027
Keep March to May free for selection interviews, since a missed interview without valid reason withdraws the application
If hostel priority matters to you, file a complete hostel application in the first housing application window each year
common_rejection_risks: Applying as a transfer student, which is an outright exclusion from this scheme
Missing a scheduled selection interview without a valid reason
Thin co-curricular or leadership evidence in a scheme that screens explicitly for leadership potential
Concurrently holding another scholarship, bursary, award or waiver without prior University approval
Slipping below the 3.50 semester GPA, or the top-80% cohort grade for Dentistry, Law and Medicine, and losing renewal
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living expenses (food, transport, books, personal), hostel fees since accommodation priority is consideration rather than a fee waiver, and any costs attached to the exchange semester; NUS publishes no living allowance or travel funding for this tier.
document_audit: The co-curricular activities record is the only supporting document named; make it evidence leadership and impact rather than a bare list of activities
The Referee Recommendation Form is submitted by your principal or tutor through the Referee Portal, not by you; confirm it was actually filed before 2 April 2027
Your admission application must exist before the scholarship application opens to you, so start it first
alerts: One application covers all three NUS Scholarships tiers and the committee places you, so the same effort can carry you to the higher tiers
Outcomes arrive by late May, after many admission-offer response windows; time your offer responses so a pending scholarship decision does not force a premature choice
Withdrawing from NUS or terminating the scholarship prematurely allows the University to require repayment of all scholarship monies disbursed
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission application first, then the common scholarship form in the Applicant Portal (1 February to 19 March 2027) with co-curricular documents uploaded, referee form in by 2 April, interviews from late March, outcome by late May, then accept and sign the Letter of Acceptance and Undertaking online.
